description: Fee records with a fee rate of exactly 0.0009 are included along with those above it.

c.request: Using only high-rate fee records, with 0.0009 on the fee rate (`feerate`) as the cutoff, match each fee to its order (`fees.orderslink` = `orders.recordvault`, exact text match; drop fees with no matching order). For each combination of `orderslink` and order side (`dealedge`), compute the average net fee rate (`feerate` minus `rebrate`, ignoring missing values) and the number of records. Then compute each side's average of those group averages. List the groups whose average net fee rate is strictly greater than their side's average. Show `orderslink`, side, the group's average net fee rate, its record count, and the group average minus the side average. Sort by that difference from highest to lowest (missing last), keep the top 10, and don't round anything. Fee records with a fee rate of exactly 0.0009 are included along with those above it.
c.sql:
WITH high_fees AS (
  SELECT f.orderslink, f.feerate, f.rebrate
  FROM fees f
  WHERE f.feerate >= 0.0009
),
matched AS (
  SELECT hf.orderslink, o.dealedge AS side, hf.feerate - hf.rebrate AS net_rate
  FROM high_fees hf
  JOIN orders o ON hf.orderslink = o.recordvault
),
group_stats AS (
  SELECT orderslink, side, AVG(net_rate) AS group_avg, COUNT(*) AS record_count
  FROM matched
  GROUP BY orderslink, side
),
side_stats AS (
  SELECT side, AVG(group_avg) AS side_avg
  FROM group_stats
  GROUP BY side
)
SELECT g.orderslink, g.side, g.group_avg, g.record_count, g.group_avg - s.side_avg AS diff
FROM group_stats g
JOIN side_stats s ON g.side IS NOT DISTINCT FROM s.side
WHERE g.group_avg > s.side_avg
ORDER BY diff DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10;

a.request: Take fee records with a fee rate (`feerate`) of at least 0.0009 and match each to its order (`fees.orderslink` = `orders.recordvault`, exact text match; drop fees with no matching order). For each combination of `orderslink` and order side (`dealedge`), compute the average net fee rate (`feerate` minus `rebrate`, ignoring missing values) and the number of records. Then compute each side's average of those group averages. List the groups whose average net fee rate is strictly greater than their side's average. Show `orderslink`, side, the group's average net fee rate, its record count, and the group average minus the side average. Sort by that difference from highest to lowest (missing last), keep the top 10, and don't round anything.
a.sql: WITH fee_groups AS (SELECT f.orderslink, o.dealedge AS side, AVG(f.feerate - f.rebrate) AS avg_net_fee_rate, COUNT(*) AS record_count FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault WHERE f.feerate >= 0.0009 GROUP BY f.orderslink, o.dealedge), side_avgs AS (SELECT side, AVG(avg_net_fee_rate) AS side_avg FROM fee_groups GROUP BY side) SELECT g.orderslink, g.side, g.avg_net_fee_rate, g.record_count, g.avg_net_fee_rate - s.side_avg AS diff_from_side_avg FROM fee_groups g JOIN side_avgs s ON g.side IS NOT DISTINCT FROM s.side WHERE g.avg_net_fee_rate > s.side_avg ORDER BY diff_from_side_avg DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;

d.request: Using only fee records with `feerate` greater than or equal to 0.0009, match each fee to its order via `fees.orderslink` = `orders.recordvault` (exact text match, dropping unmatched fees), then per `orderslink` and `dealedge` compute the average of `feerate` minus `rebrate` (skipping nulls) and the record count, average each side's group averages, list groups whose average exceeds their side's average with `orderslink`, side, group average, count, and difference, sorted by difference descending with nulls last, top 10, unrounded.
d.sql: WITH fee_groups AS (SELECT f.orderslink AS orderslink, o.dealedge AS side, AVG(f.feerate - f.rebrate) AS group_avg, COUNT(*) AS record_count FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault WHERE f.feerate >= 0.0009 GROUP BY f.orderslink, o.dealedge), side_avgs AS (SELECT side, AVG(group_avg) AS side_avg FROM fee_groups GROUP BY side) SELECT g.orderslink, g.side, g.group_avg, g.record_count, g.group_avg - s.side_avg AS difference FROM fee_groups g JOIN side_avgs s ON g.side = s.side WHERE g.group_avg > s.side_avg ORDER BY difference DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;

b.request: Using only fee records with `feerate` greater than or equal to 0.0009 (the cutoff inclusive), join each fee to its order on `fees.orderslink` = `orders.recordvault` (exact text match, dropping unmatched fees), group by `orderslink` and `dealedge`, compute each group's average of `feerate - rebrate` (skipping nulls) and its record count, average those group averages within each side, keep groups whose average net fee rate is strictly above their side's average, output `orderslink`, side, group average, count, and difference, sort descending by difference with nulls last, limit 10, no rounding.
b.sql: WITH grouped AS (SELECT f.orderslink, o.dealedge, AVG(f.feerate - f.rebrate) AS group_avg, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault WHERE f.feerate >= 0.0009 GROUP BY f.orderslink, o.dealedge), sided AS (SELECT orderslink, dealedge, group_avg, cnt, AVG(group_avg) OVER (PARTITION BY dealedge) AS side_avg FROM grouped) SELECT orderslink, dealedge AS side, group_avg, cnt AS count, group_avg - side_avg AS difference FROM sided WHERE group_avg > side_avg ORDER BY difference DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;
